title: Best Mini PCs for Self-Hosting AI Assistants in 2026
excerpt: Self-hosting AI assistants like OpenClaw requires hardware that's always on, quiet, and efficient. Mini PCs hit the sweet spot — powerful enough to run 24/7, small enough

content.html:
Self-hosting AI assistants like OpenClaw requires hardware that's always on, quiet, and efficient. Mini PCs hit the sweet spot — powerful enough to run 24/7, small enough to hide behind your router, and affordable enough to justify dedicated AI hardware.

Why Mini PCs for AI Self-Hosting?

Mini PCs offer unique advantages for running personal AI assistants:

  • Low power consumption: 15-35W typical vs 200W+ for a desktop
  • Silent operation: Many models are fanless or near-silent
  • Compact footprint: Fits on a shelf, behind a monitor, or mounted to a wall
  • Always-on ready: Designed for continuous operation
  • Cost-effective: Refurbished business units start around $100

What Specs Do You Need?

For API-based AI assistants (like OpenClaw with Claude or GPT-4):

ComponentMinimumRecommended
CPUIntel i3 / AMD Ryzen 3Intel i5 / AMD Ryzen 5
RAM4GB8GB+
Storage64GB SSD256GB+ SSD
OSLinux / Windows / macOSLinux (lowest overhead)

Note: If you plan to run local AI models (like Llama), you'll need significantly more RAM (32GB+) and possibly a GPU. For API-based setups, modest hardware works great.

Top Mini PC Picks for AI Self-Hosting

Best Overall: Lenovo ThinkCentre M910q

The Lenovo ThinkCentre M910q is a business-class mini PC that's perfect for always-on AI hosting.

  • Why it's great: Reliable, well-built, widely available refurbished
  • Typical specs: Intel i5-6500T/7500T, 8-16GB RAM, 256GB SSD
  • Power draw: ~20W idle
  • Best for: Reliable 24/7 operation on a budget

Best Budget: Beelink Mini S

The Beelink Mini S series offers excellent value for basic AI hosting needs.

  • Why it's great: Affordable new units, compact design
  • Typical specs: Intel N95/N100, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD
  • Power draw: ~10-15W idle
  • Best for: Budget-conscious setups, low power priority

Best Performance: Intel NUC 12/13

The Intel NUC line delivers strong performance in a tiny package.

  • Why it's great: Powerful processors, excellent build quality
  • Typical specs: Intel i5/i7 12th-13th gen, up to 64GB RAM
  • Power draw: ~25-35W idle
  • Best for: Power users, local model experiments

Best for Local AI Models: Minisforum with AMD

The Minisforum UM series with AMD processors offers the best local AI potential.

  • Why it's great: AMD APUs with strong integrated graphics
  • Typical specs: AMD Ryzen 7/9, up to 64GB RAM, Radeon iGPU
  • Power draw: ~30-45W idle
  • Best for: Running smaller local models alongside API-based AI

Setup Tips for AI Hosting

Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu or Debian) is recommended for AI hosting:

  • Lower resource overhead than Windows
  • Better command-line tooling
  • Easier headless operation
  • Free and well-documented

Network Configuration

  • Static IP: Assign a fixed local IP for reliable access
  • SSH access: Enable remote management
  • Firewall: Only open necessary ports

Power and Reliability

  • UPS recommended: A small UPS prevents data loss from power blips
  • Auto-start: Configure BIOS to boot on power restore
  • Monitoring: Set up alerts for downtime

Refurbished vs New

For budget builds, refurbished business mini PCs offer exceptional value:

Advantages of Refurbished

  • 50-70% cheaper than new equivalents
  • Business-class reliability (built for 24/7)
  • Often include warranty (90 days typical)
  • Environmentally friendly (reduces e-waste)

What to Check

  • Battery condition (if applicable)
  • RAM and storage (often upgradeable)
  • Seller reputation and return policy
  • Physical condition of ports and fans

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use a Raspberry Pi instead?

A Raspberry Pi 4/5 works for API-based AI like OpenClaw, but performance is limited. For casual use it's fine; for serious daily use, an x86 mini PC is more capable. Pi's main advantage is ultra-low power (~5W).

Do I need a GPU for OpenClaw?

No. OpenClaw uses cloud AI APIs (Claude, GPT-4), so all heavy computation happens remotely. You only need a GPU if running local AI models.

How much does it cost to run 24/7?

A 20W mini PC running 24/7 uses about 14.4 kWh per month. At $0.15/kWh, that's roughly $2.16/month in electricity — less than a single coffee.

Can I run other services alongside AI?

Yes! Most mini PCs have plenty of headroom for additional services like Home Assistant, Pi-hole, file servers, or media streaming alongside OpenClaw.

What about Mac Mini?

Mac Mini (especially M1/M2) is excellent but pricier. It runs OpenClaw beautifully and the Apple Silicon chips are very power-efficient. Great choice if you prefer macOS or already own one.

Our Recommendation

For most users self-hosting OpenClaw or similar AI assistants:

Start with a refurbished ThinkCentre M910q or similar business mini PC. They're reliable, quiet, cheap ($100-150), and more than capable for API-based AI. Upgrade to something beefier only if you want to experiment with local models.

The best AI hardware is hardware that runs reliably without you thinking about it.
